input.intent: Preserve a navigator fighting through Clima-Tact weather science, lightning, and weather deception. Consider Zeus inhabiting the Clima-Tact by the selected continuity. Build a playable kit with at least 15 meaningful purchasable upgrades that each change executable behavior. Select a coherent subset instead of claiming exhaustive coverage. Disclose omitted defining abilities and any source limits. Treat numerical damage, costs, cooldowns, range, targeting and unlock progression as explicit gameplay adaptations. Do not invent character powers to meet upgrade count; deepen sourced abilities where possible.

context.evidencePurpose: Curated development demonstration, available to generation and review; not an unseen benchmark.
context.reviewScope: Selected manga continuity through end of Wano; exclude later manga, anime-only and game-only facts from this request.
context.priorReviewCorrections: Mirage Tempo creates illusions; it does not establish sensing concealed enemies. Do not grant detection from mirages. Damage multipliers do not implement projectile steering or improved reliability. Describe their actual scope, including collateral damage.
context.descriptionAgreement: Descriptions must state the scope of the actual executable modifiers. Unsupported history dependence, target senses, recoil, movement and elemental status must remain explicit omissions.

research.subject: Nami
gaps: The supplied pages do not provide gameplay values for damage, costs, cooldowns, ranges, targeting rules, resource limits, or unlock progression. Any such values would be explicit gameplay adaptations rather than character evidence.

The request for at least 15 purchasable upgrades is a design requirement, not evidence about Nami. A kit can deepen the sourced Clima-Tact, weather, lightning, mist, heat, wind, Zeus, and Impact behaviors, but the sources do not support an exhaustive upgrade tree.

Mirage Tempo is supported as illusion and deception. The supplied evidence does not support detecting concealed enemies, revealing targets, granting senses, or improving reliability merely because an illusion or damage multiplier exists.

The source supports specific directed-lightning behavior from Nami's Clima-Tact and Zeus, but does not support treating arbitrary damage multipliers as projectile steering, homing, recoil reduction, or general accuracy improvements.
No supplied page establishes generic elemental status rules such as stun, burn, shock, slow, freeze, or damage-over-time behavior beyond the described attack outcomes and collateral harm.
Impact's drawback is supported, but the sources do not define a general recoil system for Nami's other attacks or weapons.

The supplied pages do not document movement buffs, evasive bonuses, or history-dependent gameplay mechanics. Nami's agility and speed feats should not automatically become universal movement modifiers.

The named Clima-Tact, Perfect Clima-Tact, Sorcery Clima-Tact, further upgraded second model, and Zeus-associated third model are weapon states or upgrades. No bodily transformation for Nami is supported in the supplied pages.

The abilities page contains material from after Wano, including Egghead and Elbaph feats, as well as non-canon and video-game sections. Those later or separate-continuity facts and techniques, including Mirai Kick and Kyoda, are omitted from this selected record.
The supplied material gives broad descriptions of Zeus's sentience and attack control but no precise limits on cloud duration, consciousness transfer, storage capacity, range, or vulnerability.
